questions.questionText: hour 15 minutes Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.

The government has to choose the best of four routes to build a new railway line. The benefits and costs of each are shown in $m in the table. Which route would be chosen? private external external private cost benefit benefit cost

A government is planning to intervene in a market to fix output at the socially desirable level by giving a subsidy. MSC = MPC T costs/ Y benefits S X MSB MPB O R W output To achieve its objective, what should be the subsidy per unit?

options.A: ST B SX C TY D XY

questions.questionText: The diagram shows two indifference curves and two budget lines for goods X and Y. Y H good Y F G IC IC O X X
Which act of purchase or consumption is most likely to illustrate the law of diminishing marginal utility?

options.A: the final course of an ‘eat all you can’ banquet to end an evening out
options.B: the last coin to complete an enthusiast’s coin collection
options.C: the second of the two rolls of wallpaper needed to decorate a room
options.D: the tenth driving lesson needed to enable a learner to pass the driving test

questions.questionText: Why might an industry consist mainly of small firms?

options.A: Diseconomies of scale occur at a low level of output.
options.B: Government policy encourages horizontal integration.
options.C: Integration is impossible.
options.D: There is an international market for the product.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a firm’s short-run marginal cost curve. SMC cost O Q output What explains why the curve is upward sloping at output levels above OQ?

options.A: diseconomies of scale
options.B: inelasticity of supply
options.C: rising fixed costs
options.D: the law of variable proportions

questions.questionText: The table shows average total cost and marginal cost for a firm in perfect competition for a range of output. output 1 2 3 4 5 average total cost $ 12 7.5 6 5.25 4.8 marginal cost $ 3 3 3 3 3 What can be concluded from the above information?

options.A: The firm is operating with diseconomies of scale.
options.B: The firm’s average variable cost is constant.
options.C: The firm’s fixed costs are $12.
options.D: The firm’s revenue will not cover cost for this output.

questions.questionText: What is an example of the principal-agent problem?

options.A: the disincentive effect for entrepreneurs of high government tax rates
options.B: the existence of a trade union to put forward workers’ views to managers
options.C: the lack of consumer knowledge of the quality of firms’ products
options.D: the separation of the owners of a firm from the firm’s managers

questions.questionText: A firm in monopolistic competition increases its expenditure on marketing its product. What will it not be able to achieve as a result?

options.A: a higher long-run profit
options.B: a higher selling price
options.C: a more differentiated product
options.D: a more inelastic demand

questions.questionText: A market structure in which a small number of firms face competition from potential entrants. What does this describe?

options.A: a contestable market
options.B: a monopoly
options.C: monopolistic competition
options.D: perfect oligopoly

questions.questionText: The diagram shows cost and revenue of a monopoly that decides to produce at OX. total cost total revenue cost, revenue O X output What can definitely be confirmed as the firm’s aim?

options.A: growth rate maximisation
options.B: long-run profit maximisation
options.C: sales revenue maximisation
options.D: short-run profit maximisation

questions.questionText: What is most likely to be the reason why monopolistically competitive firms are able to influence price?

options.A: The firms in the industry are able to prevent the entry of new firms when abnormal profits are earned.
options.B: The firms produce where average costs are falling and so experience excess capacity.
options.C: The output is where marginal revenue exceeds average revenue.
options.D: The products are differentiated and so are not perfect substitutes.

questions.questionText: What could not justify state intervention in an economy on grounds of ‘market failure’?

options.A: monopoly supply of certain goods
options.B: pollution of rivers
options.C: the existence of large-scale poverty
options.D: the existence of public goods

questions.questionText: Governments consider both efficiency and equity in deciding microeconomic policy. What statement about the resulting decisions is correct?

options.A: An economically inefficient outcome is certain to be inequitable.
options.B: Both efficiency and equity decisions are based on positive economic judgements.
options.C: Equity can only be achieved when incomes are redistributed equally.
options.D: The creation of an equitable situation may increase economic efficiency.

questions.questionText: The diagrams show the demand for and supply of labour in four markets.

In the diagram, the ARP curve is the average revenue product curve of labour of a profit- L maximising monopsonist and the MRP is the marginal revenue product of labour curve. L The curves AFC and MFC are the firm’s average and marginal factor cost curves. L L MFC L W AFC
What would be likely to reduce the mobility of labour between a depressed and a prosperous region of a country?

options.A: a developed market in rented accommodation in the prosperous region
options.B: a high rate of job turnover in the prosperous region
options.C: the setting of wages at a national level
options.D: the withdrawal of a statutory minimum wage

questions.questionText: The increase in a country’s labour productivity exceeds the increase in its real national output. What could explain this?

options.A: a decrease in employment
options.B: a deficit in the balance of trade
options.C: an increase in real wages
options.D: an increase in the rate of inflation

questions.questionText: The table shows the annual percentage (%) change in China’s GDP and the contribution of some of its component parts between 2006 and 2012. 2006 2007 2008 2009 2010 2011 2012 GDP 12.7 14.2 9.6 9.2 10.4 9.3 7.7 consumption 5.1 5.6 4.2 4.6 4.5 5.2 4.2 investment 5.5 6.0 4.5 8.1 5.5 4.5 3.9 net exports 2.1 2.6 0.9 –3.5 0.4 –0.4 –0.4 What can be concluded about China’s economy between 2006 and 2012?

options.A: China’s current account was in surplus more years than it was in deficit.
options.B: China’s economic rate of growth fell in more years than it rose.
options.C: China’s growth was greater overall in consumer goods than in capital goods.
options.D: China’s standard of living rose at a decreasing rate.

questions.questionText: What has been a common economic factor in countries that have developed rapidly in recent years?

options.A: decreased population
options.B: increased emphasis on government planning
options.C: increased openness to international trade and investment
options.D: increased unemployment

questions.questionText: National income statistics show that real GDP per head is 25% higher in country X than in country Y. Why might this difference exaggerate the gap in average living standards between the two countries?

options.A: Country X has a higher rate of inflation than country Y.
options.B: Country X has a larger population than country Y.
options.C: The proportion of services that people provide for themselves is higher in country Y.
options.D: The proportion of the country’s industry owned by foreign firms is higher in country Y.

questions.questionText: What might help improve economic growth in developing countries over the next five years?

options.A: an increase in income tax
options.B: an increase in the birth rate
options.C: an increase in the budget surplus
options.D: an increase in training

questions.questionText: Which explains how changes in national income may be brought about by changes in investment?

options.A: the acceleration principle
options.B: the investment function
options.C: the marginal efficiency of capital
options.D: the theory of the multiplier

questions.questionText: In a closed economy with no government, the equilibrium level of income occurs where

options.A: planned consumption is equal to desired investment.
options.B: planned consumption is equal to desired savings.
options.C: planned investment is equal to desired savings.
options.D: planned savings plus desired investment is equal to consumption.

questions.questionText: In the diagram, OP is the equilibrium level of income and OQ the full employment level of income in a closed economy. V U C + I + G expenditure T C + I R C 45° O P Q income What is the deflationary gap?

options.A: PQ B RV C TV D UV

questions.questionText: Which is most likely to cause an increase in a country’s money supply?

options.A: a balance of payments surplus
options.B: a government budget surplus
options.C: cash withdrawals by commercial bank depositors
options.D: the recall of loans by the commercial banks

questions.questionText: Unemployment in an economy increases. What is a probable consequence?

options.A: a switch from direct to indirect taxation
options.B: an increase in demand-pull inflation
options.C: an increase in the balance of trade deficit
options.D: an increase in the government budget deficit

questions.questionText: Other things being equal, what is likely to result from a decrease in interest rates?

options.A: a decrease in investment
options.B: a net capital inflow
options.C: an appreciation of the currency
options.D: an increase in consumption

questions.questionText: In the absence of offsetting factors, how will an increase in interest rates affect share prices?

options.A: It will decrease share prices because financial investors will prefer to purchase bonds.
options.B: It will decrease share prices because inflationary pressure will increase.
options.C: It will increase share prices because company profits will rise.
